text:
kate_sec: flagging a weird one: a DAST suppression auto-approved yesterday because CI reported decrypt succeeded, but central audit project has no KMS Decrypt entry for the service account in any region. we should treat cross-project decrypts as first-class evidence.
juan_dev: i inspected the CI run: decrypt happened in us-central1 and the job uses a cross-project key (projects/redwood-keys-us/...). CI stdout shows decrypt ok. snippet: 
```
2026-03-25T11:04:12Z INFO decrypt OK (ciphertext: build-secrets.enc)
```
but when i ran a quick logging read in the central audit project it returned empty.
juan_dev: run i tried:```bash
gcloud logging read 'resource.type="kms_crypto_key" AND protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail="ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"' --project=redwood-audit --limit=5 --format=json
```
kate_sec: possible causes: (1) logging sink for key project not forwarding Decrypt logs to central audit project, (2) logs are in a different resource type / region-specific resource label and the filter missed them, (3) audit config for KMS 'DATA_ACCESS' not enabled on the key project.
tom_sre: we hit (3) in past incidents. KMS decrypt events are DATA_ACCESS audit logs. many projects only enabled ADMIN_ACTIVITY. check audit config:```bash
gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-keys-us --project=redwood-keys-us --format=json
# or list audit configs
gcloud logging sinks list --project=redwood-keys-us
```
juan_dev: confirmed: the key project had only admin activity enabled in audit configs. i'll open a request to enable DATA_ACCESS for the minimal principals so we get Decrypt events.
kate_sec: two policy asks: (A) export KMS Decrypt events for all key projects to central redwood-audit BigQuery dataset (partitioned) so premerge checks can query quickly, (B) give sec-team read access to that dataset (no kms roles required).
tom_sre: operationally: we'll create a Logging sink in each key project with filter 'protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt"' pointing to redwood-audit dataset. i'll own the infra play. need infra-approver to grant sink writer role on dataset.
juan_dev: for immediate mitigation on auto-suppression, can we change the premerge rule to require either (a) local CI evidence bundle uploaded to artifacts + signed metadata OR (b) a matching Decrypt row in redwood-audit? avoids relying solely on central logs until sinks are in place.
kate_sec: yes. update premerge gate to check both sources. also add a 60s buffer after job finish before checking central logs to account for sink replication.
audit-bot: [auto] created ticket SEC-1012: "cross-project KMS decrypt visibility + premerge gating" assigned to @tom_sre, @kate_sec. link: https://github.internal/redwood/security/SEC-1012
tom_sre: I'll start a doc with the sink steps and dataset IAM checklist. plan: enable DATA_ACCESS audit logging on key projects, create sinks, grant dataset writer to sinks, grant sec-team BigQuery DataViewer on dataset, set partition expiration 90d.
kate_sec: thanks. i'll update the premerge GH Action to prefer local evidence bundle fallback and add the 60s wait. will link PR to SEC-1012.
juan_dev: one more note: log formats vary by region/resource; the GH Action should be flexible in the gcloud filter and try both resource types (kms_crypto_key and k8s_cluster) for cross-checked runs. small snippet to try both:```bash
gcloud logging read '(protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt") AND (resource.type="kms_crypto_key" OR resource.type="k8s_cluster")' --project=redwood-audit --limit=1 --format=json
```
kate_sec: perfect. we'll track metric sdlc.crossproj_missing_decrypt_total after rollout. thanks all.
